basis: Epilepsy is defined by persistent brain dysfunction; unknown seizure onset does not change the organ axis.
Intellectual disability and language delay in 9/9; ataxia, spasticity and brain abnormalities are neurologic. No established common extra-neurologic damage.
Disease of the endocardium; infection and other mechanisms apply only to particular subtypes.
Diaphragm defect with pulmonary hypoplasia and pulmonary hypertension; intestinal malrotation occurs in 30-79%.
Fixed foot deformities and amyotrophy 2/2; ovarian insufficiency 1/1 assessed female; visual acuity loss 1/2. Frequencies derive from a very small series.
Inherited vascular malformations; portal hypertension with elevated liver enzymes in 1/3 supports hepatic involvement. Epistaxis alone does not establish airway damage.
Severe developmental encephalopathy with structural brain abnormalities and defective intermediary metabolism causing lactic acidosis; respiratory insufficiency lacks intrinsic lung disease.
Defined by mandibular and limb skeletal defects together with glossoptosis and cleft palate; oral structures fall within gastrointestinal.
Defined by keratinization disease, damaging keratitis and hearing loss; dental abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Secondary skin infections do not establish primary immunodeficiency.
Cancer originates in the paraurethral gland, classified here as a vulvar reproductive organ; urethral origin or invasion is not established.
Classical complement immunodeficiency; infections and autoimmune diseases are separately diagnosed consequences. Lupus affects only about 10-20%.
Inherited ovarian cancer arises in a reproductive organ; ovarian tumour origin alone does not establish endocrine dysfunction.
Neurodegeneration causes motor, sensory and cognitive dysfunction; rigidity and movement abnormalities do not establish intrinsic skeletal muscle disease.
Adenocarcinoma originates in the fallopian tube, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Inflammatory outer-retinal disease causing visual dysfunction; presumed immune-mediated white dot syndrome, although its precise mechanism remains uncertain.
Developmental brain disorder; atrial septal defect 3/6 and ptosis/proptosis 3/6. Hypoglycemia lacks evidence of persistent endocrine damage; forehead stain is non-damaging.
Myotonic muscle disease; conduction abnormalities ~60-80%, cataracts >80%, GI smooth-muscle dysmotility >50%. CNS/endocrine manifestations omitted at the four-axis cap.
Defined by facial muscle hypoplasia. Multisystem HPO conflict with the isolated phenotype and description of less frequent associated anomalies; common direct extra-organ damage is unproven.
Leptin signalling deficiency causes obesity, hypogonadism and T-cell dysfunction (80-99%); autonomic dysfunction with orthostatic hypotension is reported in 30-79%.
Inherited cardiac conduction and rhythm disease, sometimes accompanied by dilated cardiomyopathy; all established manifestations share the cardiovascular axis.
Defined by spastic paraplegia, axonal neuropathy and optic atrophy (21/22); fixed joint contractures affect 80-99% and scoliosis 14/22.
Benign lesion of lymphatic vascular channels; the umbrella has variable tissue locations without a consistently damaged additional organ.
Immune-mediated ulcerative inflammation of the rectum and sigmoid colon; no additional organ is commonly directly damaged.
Chronic disorder of cutaneous apocrine sweat glands and surrounding skin; no established systemic immune mechanism or extra-organ injury.
Red-cell membrane disease causing spherocytosis and hemolytic anemia; splenic involvement shares this axis. Hemolytic jaundice does not establish liver damage.
